title: Sparsity of quadratic Boolean thresholds
statement: Let $n$ be a positive even integer, and let $p$ be a real-valued function on $\\{-1,1\\}^n$ whose threshold sign agrees everywhere with the complete quadratic Boolean function $x\mapsto (-1)^{\sum_{i<j}x_i x_j}$, using the identification of signs with bits in $\mathbb F_2$. Then the number of nonzero Fourier coefficients of $p$ is at least $2^{n/2}$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ represents the complete quadratic Boolean function by threshold signs
